body: Washington found just enough in a 35-28 win over Miami in Week 2 PCFL action, with Graham Mertz earning Player of the Game honors after going for 30 of 53 for 389 yards and 3 TDs.
The Huskies were outgained by Miami 404–330 in total offense, including 93 yards on the ground. Miami kept fighting, managing 404 total yards on the night.

aiStory.headline: Washington rallies from 13 down, kick returns flip field in 35-28 win
aiStory.dek: The Huskies improve to 2-0 and climb to No. 4 in the power poll while Miami falls to 0-2 and drops to No. 14.
body: With 2:19 left in the fourth quarter and Washington leading 35-21, Miami faced third-and-10 at the Washington 15 when Graham Mertz found Chimere Dike for a 15-yard touchdown that cut the deficit to seven. The extra point made it 35-28, but a 53-yard punt pinned the Hurricanes at their 23 with 1:12 remaining; two completions moved the ball to the 44 before a sack and a fourth-down scramble that lost six yards gave Washington the ball at the Miami 28 with 27 seconds to play.

Miami struck first, taking a 13-0 lead after one quarter on a Romeo Dixon touchdown run and a 10-yard Mertz-to-Gunner Benton strike. Washington answered with a 17-yard Elijah Brown-to-Rashid Williams pass late in the half, then seized momentum in the third: a 95-yard Mason James kickoff return set up a Brown quarterback sneak, a 10-play, 80-yard drive ended with a Brian Bonner Jr. plunge, and a 61-yard James return preceded a Bonner Jr. score that made it 28-13. Miami tied it at 21 on a Mertz-to-Dike one-yarder and a two-point conversion, but Washington reclaimed the lead on a Bonner Jr. one-yard run and a Demond Williams Jr.-to-James 33-yard touchdown pass that pushed the margin to 14.

The box score tells the story of two contrasting formulas: Miami piled up 404 yards, 369 through the air on Mertz's 30-of-53, 389-yard, three-touchdown effort, yet managed only 35 rushing yards and went 0-for-1 on fourth down. Washington gained 330 total yards with a balanced 93 on the ground and 237 passing, converted its lone fourth-down try, and turned two explosive kickoff returns — 95 and 61 yards by James — into a 14-point swing. The Hurricanes' lone turnover, a Mertz interception by Emmanuel Karnley in the second quarter, stalled a drive inside Washington territory, while the Huskies played turnover-free football.

The loss drops Miami to 0-2 overall and 0-2 in the Eastern Southern, extending a two-game skid and sliding the program from No. 10 to No. 14 in the power poll; the Hurricanes now host unbeaten USC next week. Washington improves to 2-0 and 2-0 in the Western Pacific, riding a two-game winning streak to No. 4 in the poll and a share of the division lead with USC; the Huskies travel to Arizona State looking to stay perfect.
aiStory.turningPoint: The 95-yard kickoff return by Mason James to open the third quarter set up Washington's first touchdown and ignited a 21-0 run that erased a 13-point deficit.
byTheNumbers: Miami outgained Washington 404-330 but rushed for only 35 yards, leaving the offense one-dimensional and vulnerable to third-down pressure.
Washington converted 5 of 11 third downs (45%) and its only fourth-down attempt, while Miami went 10 of 15 (67%) on third down but failed on its lone fourth-down try in the final minute.
Mason James produced 103 receiving yards and a touchdown plus 170 kickoff-return yards on two returns, accounting for 273 all-purpose yards and two explosive plays of 60-plus yards.
Graham Mertz threw for 389 yards and three touchdowns — second in the league this week only to the season leader — but the interception and fourth-down failure in the closing seconds proved costly.

unsungHero.name: Brian Bonner Jr.
unsungHero.why: Scored two short-yardage rushing touchdowns on consecutive third-quarter drives that turned field position from Mason James' kick returns into a 14-point lead swing.

The Fighting Irish outgained Arkansas 478–310 in total offense, including 145 yards on the ground. Arkansas kept fighting, managing 310 total yards on the night.
Up next, Notre Dame hosts Georgia in Week 3.

aiStory.headline: Notre Dame strikes early and often in 35-10 rout of Arkansas
aiStory.dek: The Fighting Irish move to 1-1 and hand the Razorbacks their first loss, reshaping both division races ahead of Week 3.
body: Notre Dame struck first at 12:52 of the opening quarter when CJ Carr handed off to Ricky Watters for a short touchdown run that capped a four-play, 78-yard drive and made it 7-0. The Irish never relinquished the lead, pushing the margin to 32 points on Hollywood Smothers' second rushing score at 13:33 of the fourth quarter.

Notre Dame scored on its first four possessions — Watters and Smothers on the ground in the first quarter, then Carr-to-Golden Tate and Carr-to-William Fuller through the air in the second — building a 28-0 halftime cushion. Arkansas answered with a Cruz Gibson 47-yard field goal at 4:33 of the third and a Mike Washington one-yard plunge at 6:45 of the fourth, but the damage was long since done. There were no lead changes; Notre Dame's largest lead reached 32 points early in the final period.

Carr finished 24-of-39 for 357 yards and two touchdowns despite three interceptions, while Smothers added 62 yards and two scores on 14 carries. Notre Dame converted 7 of 14 third downs and held the ball for 34:02, outgaining Arkansas 478-310 overall and 145-86 on the ground. The Razorbacks managed just 15 first downs and went 0-for-11 on third down; K.J. Jackson threw for 249 yards on 13-of-30 passing with no touchdowns, and Frederick Clay led all receivers with 91 yards on four catches. Arkansas's defense forced three picks — Jared Bullock, Colten Conrad and Fabio Duke each had one — but the offense could not capitalize.

Arkansas falls to 1-1 and drops from the top of the power poll to No. 10, sitting third in the Eastern Southern behind division leader LSU. Notre Dame improves to 1-1 and climbs to No. 6 in the poll, fourth in the Western Central with Michigan atop the division. The Razorbacks host Penn State (1-1) next week; the Irish welcome Georgia (0-2).
aiStory.turningPoint: Notre Dame's 97-yard, nine-play touchdown drive capped by Hollywood Smothers' short run at 5:47 of the first quarter made it 14-0 and set the tone for a wire-to-wire win.
byTheNumbers: Third-down conversion rate: Notre Dame 50% (7/14) vs. Arkansas 0% (0/11) — the Irish sustained drives while the Razorbacks could not stay on the field.
Time of possession: Notre Dame 34:02 to Arkansas 25:58 — a nearly nine-minute edge that wore down the Arkansas defense and limited Jackson's opportunities.
Rushing yards: Notre Dame 145 vs. Arkansas 86 — Smothers contributed 62 yards and two touchdowns on the ground, helping control the line of scrimmage.
Turnover margin: Arkansas forced three interceptions but scored only three points on the day; Notre Dame committed three picks yet still won by 25.

unsungHero.name: Golden Tate
unsungHero.why: Caught a 30-yard explosive play at 14:50 of the first quarter and the 8-yard touchdown that made it 21-0, then added a 17-yard grab on the final Irish possession — three first-down receptions that kept chains moving.

aiStory.headline: MacIntyre, Merritt Spark Tennessee Past Penn State 26-20
aiStory.dek: Tennessee stays unbeaten and atop the power poll while Penn State drops its first game and falls to tenth.
body: With 1:18 left in the fourth quarter and Tennessee clinging to a 26-20 lead, backup quarterback Jake Merklinger faced third-and-35 from his own 4-yard line and uncorked a 51-yard strike to Radarious Jackson that flipped the field and let the Volunteers drain the clock.

Tennessee struck first on a Brad Maddox 38-yard field goal at 11:26 of the first quarter, then surged ahead 11-0 when George MacIntyre hit Joakim Dodson for a 6-yard touchdown and the two-point conversion early in the second. Maddox added a 30-yarder to make it 14-0 before Penn State answered with a Mark Vaughn 3-yard touchdown run at 1:26. Maddox closed the half with a 19-yard field goal for a 17-7 lead. Penn State trimmed the margin to 17-10 on a Yousef Joseph 45-yarder to open the third, but MacIntyre capped an 11-play, 79-yard drive with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Braylon Staley for a 23-10 edge. Joseph hit another 45-yarder to cut it to 23-13, then Maddox pushed the lead to 26-13 with a 35-yard field goal at 8:40 of the fourth. Myers found Omari Evans for a 6-yard touchdown at 2:28 to make it a one-score game, but the Volunteers recovered the ensuing onside kick and Merklinger's explosive completion to Jackson iced the outcome.

The box score tells the story: Tennessee outgained Penn State 398 yards to 281, converted 64 percent of third downs to 58 percent, and won the turnover battle 1-0 behind Timothy Merritt's 31-yard interception return of a Myers pass intended for Jay Edwards at 2:38 of the first quarter. MacIntyre finished 21 of 28 for 278 yards and two touchdowns, pushing his season total to 725 yards and keeping him atop the PCFL passing leaderboard. Penn State's Myers threw for 199 yards and a score but absorbed three sacks in the final two minutes, while the Nittany Lions managed just 88 rushing yards on the day. Tennessee's 33:05 time of possession and 4-30 penalty margin reflected the control the Volunteers exerted throughout.

The win moves Tennessee to 2-0 with a two-game winning streak and keeps the Volunteers at No. 1 in the power poll, sitting second in the Eastern Southern behind division leader LSU. Penn State falls to 1-1, drops from No. 1 to No. 10 in the poll, and falls a game behind Texas in the Eastern Atlantic. Next week Tennessee travels to face Ohio State (1-1) while Penn State visits Arkansas (1-1) looking to right the ship.
aiStory.turningPoint: Merritt's interception at 2:38 of the first quarter gave Tennessee the ball in Penn State territory and sparked the 17-0 run that defined the game.
byTheNumbers: Tennessee 7-of-11 on third down (64%) vs. Penn State 7-of-12 (58%) — the Volunteers sustained drives while the Nittany Lions stalled.
Turnover margin 1-0 Tennessee: Merritt's 31-yard interception return was the game's only takeaway and set up a field goal.
MacIntyre 21-of-28, 278 yards, 2 TD — his 725 season yards lead the PCFL and his efficiency kept the chains moving.
Time of possession 33:05 to 26:55 — Tennessee controlled tempo and limited Penn State's offensive opportunities.

unsungHero.name: Brad Maddox
unsungHero.why: Made all four field-goal attempts from 38, 30, 19 and 35 yards, providing 12 points that proved decisive in a six-point win.

aiStory.headline: Anderson's Late Surge Powers Colorado Past Georgia 42-28
aiStory.dek: Colorado evens its record at 1-1 while Georgia falls to 0-2 in the Eastern Southern cellar.
body: With 1:25 left and Colorado clinging to a 35-28 lead, Roger Anderson handed off to Benjamin Sweeney on third-and-short from the Georgia 16; Sweeney burst through the line for a 16-yard touchdown that pushed the margin to 42-28 and effectively sealed the game.

Georgia struck first on a 17-yard strike from TJ Giles to Colbie Young at the 10:00 mark of the first quarter, but Colorado answered 1:47 later when Anderson found Everett Payne for a 26-yard score. The Buffs took their first lead early in the second on a one-yard plunge by Mike Van Horne, only for Georgia to reel off two touchdowns — a 10-yard Giles-to-Marc Williams connection and a four-yard shovel to Jimmy Campbell — to lead 21-14 at halftime. Colorado leveled it at 21 on another Van Horne run midway through the third, then exploded for three fourth-quarter touchdowns: a short Payne catch, a 27-yard dart to Silas Bolden, and the decisive Sweeney run.

Anderson finished 24 of 38 for 350 yards and three touchdowns, lifting his season total to 662 yards and six scores — third in the PCFL — while Colorado's offense rolled up 462 yards against a Georgia defense allowing 472 per game, 17th in the league. Georgia's Giles threw for 254 yards and four scores but was intercepted once by Shilo Sanders, and the Bulldogs managed only 142 rushing yards to Colorado's 117 despite holding the ball for 33:38. The Buffs converted 50 percent of third downs and both fourth-down tries, and a 51-yard Anderson-to-Alton Mecum connection in the fourth quarter set up the go-ahead score.

The win moves Colorado to 1-1, keeps them second in the Western Central behind Michigan, and extends their winning streak to one; Georgia drops to 0-2, sits last in the Eastern Southern division behind leader LSU, and has lost two straight. Next week the Bulldogs travel to face Notre Dame (1-1) while Colorado returns home to host Boston College (0-2).
aiStory.turningPoint: Q4 1:25 — Benjamin Sweeney's 16-yard touchdown run on third-and-short gave Colorado a 42-28 lead.
byTheNumbers: Anderson's 350 passing yards pushed his season total to 662, third in the PCFL behind only Geor MacIntyre's 725.
Georgia held a 33:38 to 26:22 time-of-possession edge but was outgained 462-393, highlighting Colorado's explosive efficiency.
Zero penalties for Colorado against one for Georgia; the clean sheet helped the Buffs sustain drives without self-inflicted setbacks.
Colorado converted 6 of 12 third downs (50%) and both fourth-down attempts, while Georgia went 7 of 15 on third down and 4 of 4 on fourth down.

unsungHero.name: Mike Van Horne
unsungHero.why: Scored two short-yardage touchdowns and churned out key carries on the game-clinching drive, providing the ground balance that let Anderson attack downfield.

aiStory.headline: Nussmeier, Cake Strike With 10 Seconds Left to Steal 27-24 Win
aiStory.dek: LSU improves to 2-0 and drops to fourth in the power poll while Arizona State falls to 0-2 in the Western Pacific.
body: Fourth and goal at the Arizona State 17, ten seconds on the clock, LSU trailing 24-20 — Garrett Nussmeier stood tall in a collapsing pocket and found Scott Cake streaking across the back of the end zone for a 17-yard touchdown that flipped the score to 27-24. Lilian Munoz drilled the extra point as time expired, and the Tigers walked off the field with a victory that felt impossible thirty seconds earlier.

Arizona State struck first blood on a 16-yard strike from Brock Thomas to Gary Bryant for a 7-3 lead late in the opening quarter, but a Jakailin Johnson interception returned 34 yards to the one-yard line set up Nussmeier's two-yard dart to Webb Jax that put LSU up 10-7 at the half. The Sun Devils answered with a field goal to tie it, then a 21-yard Munoz boot nudged the Tigers ahead 13-10. Thomas hit Tez Johnson from 11 yards to make it 17-13 early in the fourth, Nussmeier countered with a 20-yard laser to Cake for a 20-17 edge, and Thomas found Johnson again from five yards with 1:09 remaining to push Arizona State in front 24-20 — setting the stage for the final 53-second, 65-yard march.

The box score tells a story of Arizona State controlling the ball — 355 yards to 250, 21 first downs to 18, a 61 percent third-down clip against 23 percent — yet the Sun Devils coughed up the only turnover, a Thomas pick that handed LSU a first-and-goal at the one. Nussmeier made the most of his 212 yards and three scores, pushing his season line to 416 yards, five touchdowns and zero interceptions, while Cake's 117-yard, two-touchdown night vaulted him to third in the league with 172 receiving yards. Arizona State's defense notched three sacks from Mothudi, but the Tigers converted both fourth-down tries and committed only three penalties for 20 yards, the cleaner operation when the margin vanished.

LSU moves to 2-0 atop the Eastern Southern despite slipping from first to fourth in the power poll, averaging 32.5 points while the defense yields 388 yards a game — ninth in the league. Arizona State drops to 0-2 and fourth in the Western Pacific, the power poll tumbling from tenth to fourteenth, with the offense averaging 343.5 yards but the defense allowing 376. Next week the Tigers travel to Michigan (1-1), while the Sun Devils host unbeaten Washington.
aiStory.turningPoint: Fourth and goal at the Arizona State 17 with ten seconds left in the fourth quarter, Nussmeier hit Cake for a 17-yard touchdown to make it 27-24.
byTheNumbers: Arizona State dominated time of possession 31:09 to 28:51 and converted 11 of 18 third downs, yet the lone turnover — a Thomas interception returned 34 yards — directly produced LSU's first touchdown.
LSU gained only 250 total yards, 17th of 18 teams this week, but Nussmeier's 212 passing yards and three touchdowns yielded a ruthless efficiency.
Cake's 117 receiving yards on seven catches accounted for the bulk of LSU's passing production and lifted his season total to 172 yards, third in the PCFL.
Both teams were perfect on fourth down (2-for-2 and 1-for-1), but LSU's two conversions included the game-winning drive while Arizona State's lone try came on a successful fourth-down attempt.

unsungHero.name: Jakailin Johnson
unsungHero.why: His 34-yard interception return in the second quarter gave LSU first-and-goal at the one, setting up the touchdown that erased Arizona State's early lead and shifted momentum before halftime.

aiStory.headline: Cortez, Alabama survive Leavitt's rally, 21-20
aiStory.dek: Alabama evens its record at 1-1 while Boston College falls to 0-2 in the Eastern Atlantic race.
body: With 35 seconds left and Boston College at the Alabama 35, Darius Rivas lined up a 52-yard field goal to steal it, but the kick sailed wide right and Alabama took over at its 42 with five seconds remaining to seal a 21-20 win.

The first quarter produced only punts and a pair of missed field goals, then Alabama struck twice in the second quarter: James Cortez hit Adrian Curry on a five-yard touchdown pass at 9:42, and after Sam Leavitt answered with a seven-yard strike to Sedmaj Flemming, Cortez found Ethan Monroe on a one-yard jet sweep at 1:52 for a 14-7 halftime lead. Boston College trimmed it to 14-10 on a 33-yard Rivas field goal early in the third, but Cortez capped an 8-play, 74-yard drive with a 21-yard Keith Adams Jr. touchdown run at 5:01 to push the margin to 11. Leavitt drove the Eagles 80 yards in 13 plays for a one-yard touchdown pass to Will Graves III at 8:34 of the fourth, then a short field set up a 26-yard Rivas field goal at 4:20 to make it a one-point game.

Alabama won despite being outgained 405-345 and holding the ball barely 27 minutes, because Cortez was efficient at 19-of-30 for 252 yards and a touchdown while Leavitt needed 47 throws for 292 yards and two scores. The Tide converted just 3 of 10 third downs but went 1-for-1 on fourth down and committed zero penalties, while Boston College was 7-of-15 on third down and 2-for-2 on fourth down but left nine points on the board with three missed field goals. Adams Jr. added 40 rushing yards and the go-ahead touchdown, and Earle Hampton caught five passes for 76 yards, while Leavitt's top target Jayden Skeete finished with four catches for 62 yards and a 34-yard explosive play late in the first half.

The victory lifts Alabama to 1-1 and keeps it third in the Eastern Atlantic behind division leader Texas, while Boston College drops to 0-2 and last in the division with its power-poll ranking sliding from 10 to 14. Alabama's defense, still last in the league at 502 yards allowed per game, bent but forced the final miss, and the staff will prepare for a home date against 0-2 Michigan State next week. Boston College must regroup on the road at 1-1 Colorado, where Bo MacCormick's 107 rushing yards on the season will be needed to jumpstart an offense that ranks 16th in total yards.
aiStory.turningPoint: Rivas' 52-yard field goal attempt with nine seconds left in the fourth quarter sailed wide right, preserving Alabama's 21-20 lead.
byTheNumbers: Alabama converted 1 of 1 fourth downs while Boston College went 2 of 2, but the Tide's lone conversion came on the game's final drive to ice the clock.
Boston College missed three field goals (47, 45, 52 yards) totaling nine points, the exact margin of Alabama's largest lead.
Cortez averaged 8.4 yards per attempt with zero interceptions; Leavitt averaged 6.2 yards per attempt on 17 more throws.
The Eagles held a 32:27 to 27:33 time-of-possession edge and a 21-20 first-down advantage but turned neither into a lead.

unsungHero.name: Jason Nash
unsungHero.why: The safety knocked down Leavitt's third-down pass intended for Reed Harris and tackled Nedrick Bolden on the ensuing first-down play, forcing the fourth-down conversion that set up the final field-goal attempt.

aiStory.headline: Manning's four scores lift Texas past Ohio State 29-15
aiStory.dek: Texas moves to 2-0 and takes the Eastern Atlantic lead while Ohio State falls to 1-1 and drops to sixth in the power poll.
body: Fourth quarter, 11:31 remaining. Texas ball, first and 10 at their own 5. Arch Manning drops back, scans, and hits Amari Niblack on a quick slant for a 5-yard touchdown. The extra point makes it 29-12 Texas, a 17-point cushion that proves insurmountable. Ohio State answers with a 16-play, 71-yard march that ends in a Jayden Fielding field goal at 5:18, but a Julian Sayin interception by Jonah Williams at 2:50 and a failed fourth-down stop at the 9-yard line with 1:00 left seal a 29-15 final.

Ohio State struck first on a 13-play, 73-yard opening drive capped by Fielding's 31-yard field goal for a 3-0 lead. The Buckeyes extended it to 9-0 early in the second quarter when CJ Donaldson broke a 31-yard touchdown run. Texas responded with an 11-play, 77-yard drive finished by Manning's 10-yard strike to Parker Livingstone and a successful two-point conversion, cutting the gap to 9-8. Fielding's 41-yard field goal made it 12-8 at halftime. The third quarter flipped the game: Manning hit Rett Anderson for a 41-yard touchdown 31 seconds into the half, then found Anderson again from 8 yards out at 4:49 to push Texas ahead 22-12. Manning's fourth touchdown pass, the 5-yarder to Niblack, opened the fourth quarter and put the game away.

The numbers tell the story of efficiency versus volume. Ohio State outgained Texas 421 yards to 370 and held the ball for 32:45, but converted only 6 of 18 third downs and went 4-for-7 on fourth down, failing three times in the third quarter alone. Texas, by contrast, converted 5 of 10 third downs and its lone fourth-down attempt, while Manning completed 18 of 29 passes for 272 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions. Sayin threw for 345 yards on 30-of-59 passing but was picked off once and lost a fumble. Donaldson led Ohio State with 51 rushing yards and a score on five carries; Anderson paced Texas with five catches for 84 yards and two touchdowns. The turnover margin was even at one apiece.

Texas improves to 2-0, climbs to second in the power poll, and sits alone atop the Eastern Atlantic division with a two-game winning streak. Ohio State falls to 1-1, drops from first to sixth in the poll, and falls to third in the Western Central behind division-leading Michigan. The Buckeyes' offense, averaging 28.5 points and 438 yards per game entering the week, was held to 15 points and 421 yards; their defense, allowing 24 points per game, gave up 29. Texas's defense, ranked first in the league at 305.5 yards allowed per game, held Ohio State to 370. Next week, Ohio State hosts unbeaten Tennessee while Texas travels to UCLA.
aiStory.turningPoint: Third quarter, 13:17 — Arch Manning's 41-yard touchdown pass to Rett Anderson on the opening drive of the half gave Texas its first lead at 15-12.
byTheNumbers: Third-down conversion: Texas 50% (5/10) vs Ohio State 33% (6/18) — Texas sustained drives; Ohio State stalled.
Fourth-down attempts: Ohio State 4/7, Texas 1/1 — three Buckeye failures in the third quarter gave Texas short fields.
Arch Manning: 18/29, 272 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT — season totals rise to 524 yards, 7 TD, 0 INT, rating 123.4.
Time of possession: Ohio State 32:45, Texas 27:15 — Buckeyes controlled the clock but not the scoreboard.

unsungHero.name: Rett Anderson
unsungHero.why: Caught two of Manning's four touchdown passes, including the 41-yard strike that gave Texas its first lead, and finished with five receptions for 84 yards.

story.headline: Michigan steamrolls UCLA, 51-28
body: Michigan dominated from start to finish in a 51-28 rout over UCLA in Week 2 PCFL action, with Nico Iamaleava earning Player of the Game honors after going for 30 of 46 for 368 yards and 4 TDs.
The Wolverines outgained UCLA 519–479 in total offense, including 183 yards on the ground. UCLA kept fighting, managing 479 total yards on the night.
Up next, Michigan hosts LSU in Week 3.

aiStory.headline: Browne's five-touchdown night powers Michigan past UCLA 51-28
aiStory.dek: Both teams even their records at 1-1 and climb to sixth in the power poll with division implications looming.
body: The game's final statement arrived with 27 seconds left in the fourth quarter when Tommie Browne handed to Eric Brock at the 50 and the back burst 42 yards for a touchdown that made it 51-28, capping a three-play, 50-yard drive that took just 26 seconds.

Michigan struck first on the opening drive when Calvin Wendtland raced 29 yards for a score at 13:02 of the first quarter, and the Wolverines never trailed; UCLA answered with a 13-yard Nico Iamaleava-to-Marcus Harris strike to tie it at 7, but Michigan reeled off 20 straight points — a Vince Burkett plunge, a 25-yard Browne-to-Steve Gardner connection, and a Brock one-yard run — to lead 27-7 at halftime; the Bruins cut it to 27-14 on a Kenneth Moore III five-yard catch early in the third, yet a Herbie Swanson field goal and a Wendtland three-yard touchdown after a UCLA fumble pushed the margin to 37-14; Leland Smith caught two late Iamaleava touchdowns sandwiched around a Browne-to-Jakob Salas four-yard score before Brock's closing dash sealed the 23-point final margin.

The box score shows mirror-image first-down totals at 28 apiece and nearly identical yardage — Michigan 519, UCLA 479 — but the difference lived in the ground game and ball security: Michigan rushed for 183 yards and two Brock touchdowns against 111 for UCLA, converted 67 percent of third downs to UCLA's 63 percent, and committed zero turnovers while the Bruins lost two fumbles, one by Jalen Berger in the second quarter and one by Iamaleava in the third that set up a short Michigan touchdown drive; Iamaleava still threw for 368 yards and four scores, lifting his season total to 646 yards and 10 touchdowns with zero interceptions and a 138.5 rating that ranks fourth in the PCFL, while Browne added 336 yards and two passing scores plus two rushing touchdowns from his backs to reach 467 yards and a 98.5 rating on the year.

Both squads move to 1-1 and rise from tenth to sixth in the power poll; UCLA sits third in the Western Pacific behind division leader USC with a loss on its streak, while Michigan claims the Western Central lead at 1-1 with a win streak of one; the Bruins host unbeaten Texas next week and the Wolverines welcome unbeaten LSU, matchups that will test whether either defense — UCLA allowing 405.5 yards per game and Michigan 467 — can slow the league's top offenses.
aiStory.turningPoint: UCLA's fumble at its own 26-yard line early in the fourth quarter (Q4 14:21) gave Michigan a short field that Wendtland converted for a 37-14 lead, effectively putting the game out of reach.
byTheNumbers: Turnover margin: Michigan 0, UCLA 2 lost fumbles — the Bruins' two giveaways directly preceded 10 Michigan points and swung field position decisively.
Rushing advantage: Michigan 183 yards to UCLA 111, with Eric Brock's 80 yards and two scores providing a dimension the Bruins could not match.

Third-down efficiency: Michigan 6-of-9 (67%) versus UCLA 5-of-8 (63%) — the Wolverines sustained drives while the Bruins stalled on key possessions, including a fourth-down stop at the Michigan 42 in the third quarter.

Quarterback season arcs: Iamaleava's 10 touchdown passes rank fourth in the PCFL; Browne's 467 passing yards rank ninth, but his offense's balance produced 51 points against a defense allowing 36 per game entering the night.

unsungHero.name: Eric Brock
unsungHero.why: Rushed for 80 yards and two touchdowns on just eight carries, including the decisive 42-yard scoring run in the final minute that turned a comfortable lead into a rout.

story.headline: USC survives Michigan State by 3 in thriller
body: USC found just enough in a 35-32 thriller over Michigan State in Week 2 PCFL action, with Arnold Glass earning Player of the Game honors after going for 30 of 46 for 388 yards and 3 TDs.
The Trojans outgained Michigan State 526–445 in total offense, including 91 yards on the ground. Michigan State kept fighting, managing 445 total yards on the night.
Up next, USC travels to face Miami in Week 3.

aiStory.headline: Lynch 52-Yarder Lifts USC Past Michigan State 35-32
aiStory.dek: USC improves to 2-0 atop the Western Pacific while Michigan State falls to 0-2 and slides to No. 14 in the power poll.
body: With the game tied at 32, USC took over at its own 20 and Miller Moss hit Langston Mack for 24 yards and Kyle Ford for 21 on consecutive completions to reach the Michigan State 35. Denis Lynch then drilled a 52-yard field goal as the clock hit :13 in the fourth quarter, putting the Trojans ahead 35-32 for the final margin.

USC struck first when Rodney Linville scored on a short run at 7:36 of the first quarter to make it 7-0. Michigan State answered at :45 on a 42-yard strike from Arnold Glass to Cedric McNeil. The Trojans surged ahead 21-7 in the second quarter on a 53-yard Moss-to-Connor Burnett touchdown at 15:00 and a 98-yard drive capped by a 10-yard Moss-to-Milo Beard score at 1:58. A Keith Rocha field goal made it 21-10 at the half. Michigan State erupted for 22 unanswered points in the third quarter: a 25-yard Glass-to-Toi Bernard touchdown and two-point conversion at 10:16, a 22-yard Glass-to-McNeil strike at 8:44, and a 21-yard Sam Franklin run at 1:27 put the Spartans up 32-21. USC responded with a Lynch 44-yard field goal at 11:30 of the fourth and a Carter Myers touchdown run with a two-point conversion at 4:56 to tie it at 32, setting up Lynch's game-winner.

The box score tells the story of two aerial attacks: Moss threw for 439 yards and two touchdowns on 25-of-48 passing, while Glass countered with 388 yards and three scores on 30-of-46. Burnett led all receivers with eight catches for 201 yards and a touchdown, pushing his season total to 288 yards and the PCFL lead. Myers added 66 rushing yards and a score, raising his league-best rushing total to 152 yards. USC converted 7 of 16 third downs and both fourth-down attempts, while Michigan State went 4-for-11 on third down and did not attempt a fourth-down conversion. The lone turnover — a Rob Wilcots fumble recovered by Anthony Lucas in the first quarter — did not produce points for USC. Penalties were minimal: Michigan State 1 for 5 yards, USC 3 for 25.

USC moves to 2-0, holds the No. 2 spot in the power poll and leads the Western Pacific division. Michigan State drops to 0-2, falls to No. 14 and sits last in the Western Central at 0-2. The Spartans allowed 35 points in this game after allowing 30 per game entering the week, while the offense averaged 25 points per game entering and scored 32 here. Next week, Michigan State visits Alabama (1-1) and USC travels to Miami (0-2).
aiStory.turningPoint: Denis Lynch's 52-yard field goal at Q4 :13 broke a 32-32 tie and gave USC the lead for good.
byTheNumbers: USC outgained Michigan State 526-445 in total yards, with Moss (439 passing) and Glass (388) combining for 827 yards through the air.
Connor Burnett's 201 receiving yards gave him 288 on the season, the PCFL lead; Carter Myers' 66 rushing yards pushed him to 152, also tops in the league.
USC converted 44% of third downs (7/16) and both fourth-down tries; Michigan State converted 36% (4/11) with no fourth-down attempts.
The only turnover was a Michigan State fumble lost in Q1; neither team threw an interception.

unsungHero.name: Milo Beard
unsungHero.why: Caught a 10-yard touchdown pass to cap a 98-yard drive that gave USC a 21-7 lead late in the first half, and added a 12-yard catch on the final drive before a penalty wiped it out.

weeklyWrap.headline: Top Teams Fall as Week Two Shakes Power Poll
weeklyWrap.subhead: Five of the top six teams in the preseason power poll lost, crowning new leaders and exposing early flaws.
weeklyWrap.lead: The preseason hierarchy collapsed in Week Two as five of the top six teams in the power poll suffered defeats. Tennessee and LSU emerged as the only unbeatens left standing at the top, while USC and Texas tumbled from a shared No. 1 to a shared No. 2 after road losses.

segments.title: Volunteers Topple Nittany Lions in Statement Road Win
segments.body: Tennessee seized control early, leading 17-7 at the half and pushing the margin to 14 points in the third quarter. Penn State never led and fell to 1-1, dropping nine spots in the power poll to No. 10, while the Volunteers claimed the No. 1 ranking at 2-0.

segments.title: Longhorns and Trojans Crash the Preseason Party
segments.body: Texas dominated the second half against Ohio State, outscoring the Buckeyes 21-3 after trailing by four at the break to win by 14. USC survived a 22-point third-quarter deficit at Michigan State, rallying for a 35-32 win, but both preseason co-No. 1s fell to No. 2 in the poll.

segments.title: Buffaloes Explode for 28 Fourth-Quarter Points
segments.body: Tied 21-21 entering the final period, Colorado erupted for three lead changes and 21 unanswered points to stun Georgia 42-28. The Buffaloes improved to 1-1 while handing the Bulldogs an 0-2 start and a 14-point drop in the power poll.

segments.title: Wolverines Unleash Offensive Fury on Bruins
segments.body: Michigan scored 27 first-half points and never trailed, rolling to a 51-28 victory that vaulted them from No. 10 to a share of No. 6. UCLA, a preseason top-10 team, fell to 1-1 and tumbled to No. 14 after allowing the most points of the week.

segments.title: Tigers and Volunteers Stand Alone at 2-0
segments.body: LSU edged Arizona State 27-24 in a game featuring six lead changes, while Tennessee won at Penn State, leaving them as the only 2-0 teams among the preseason top six. Washington also sits 2-0 and rose to No. 4 after holding off Miami.

weeklyWrap.closer: With the preseason favorites scattered, Week Three matchups will test whether Tennessee and LSU can hold the top spots or if the poll chaos continues.
